title: Usd To Unreal Engine Chaos Cloth Workflow
description:
Welcome to the tutorial on USD to Unreal Engine Chaos Cloth Workflow
- In this video we will go through the necessary steps of setup and export garments from Marvelous Designer in USD file format.  And go over the workflow on how to create cloth assets in Unreal Editor for the Marvelous Designer garment exported.

You can find more information on the features mentioned in the video in the links bellow:
USD file Compatibility:
https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/17992636378777-USD-file-Compatibility-Ver-12-1
USD Export: Garment Simulation Data Option:
https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/31575287754393-USD-Export-Garment-Simulation-Data-Option-2024-0-173
18 default MetaHuman body types supported:
https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/31574389607193--Library-18-default-MetaHuman-body-types-supported-ver-2024-0-173

transcript: Welcome to the tutorial on USD to Unreal Engine Chaos Cloth Pipeline. In this marvelous designer scene, I have fitted this dress created from the previous tutorial to MetaHuman Female Medium Normal Weight Body Type. You can import default MetaHuman body types from the library. To optimize this garment for real-time simulation in Unreal Engine, increase the particle distance value to decrease mesh density. You can also add more collision thickness for the garment in Marvelous Designer. This value can be outputted with the USD file and use in Unreal Engine. Increase add thickness rendering value to add more thickness for the render mesh. Turn on simulation to drape the garment with the modified properties. Go to File ExportUSD. A render mesh with thickness and a separate single-sided simulation mesh are generated for each full garment during the USD export. In the render mesh, in the pop-up window, leave select all avatars on check and chose multiple objects and thick option. Make sure you have layout UV for the garment and turn on unified UV coordinates option. We have added a checkbox to choose whether to include the necessary garment simulation data in the output, which can be used for simulation setup in Unreal Engine Chaos Cloth. Go to Unreal Editor. Add a cloth asset, a data flow asset with a default node graph preset is automatically created. Double-click to open up the data flow node graph. Following the preset steps, first, import the USD file exported from Marvelous Designer. You can use the transform positions node to modify translation, rotation, and scale for render mesh and simulation mesh. Next, select a skeletal mesh to transfer the skin weights to the simulation mesh in the transfer skin weights node. Paint the max distance using the add weight node. Max distance informs how far the simulated cloth can move away from its animated skin position. You can weight paint in 2D and 3D. The 2D layout follows the same pattern layout in the 2D window in Marvelous Designer. So make sure not to place the pattern pieces too close or on top of each other before export. Smooth the weight and click the Accept button. You can remap the max distance range by changing low and high value in simulation max distance config node. The simulation config nodes are used to set the fabric settings for the cloth materials. By default, they are set to ingest the Marvelous Designer fabric parameters, but you can always use custom value for each parameter. The first blue toggle will enable the use of Marvelous Designer values, and the shirt icon will enable the weight map based on fabrics assigned in Marvelous Designer. Next, select a physics asset in the Set Physics Asset node. Double check if the physics asset has been correctly set up. In Preview Scene Detail tab, select a skeletal mesh asset to preview the simulation. Click the Toggle Simulation suspended button to toggle simulation on and off, and click one of the Reset Simulation button to reset the garment to the imported state. By default, self-collision is disabled. You can set simulation self-collision spheres config node active, or use simulation self-collision config node to create more costly and precise self-collision. Configurate the iterations and sub-steps of the cloth simulation in the Simulation Solver config node. Set up wind force in the Simulation Aerodynamics config node. In Simulation Collision config node, we are going to turn on the blue toggle for collision thickness. To use the value in the USD file, export it from Marvelous Designer. Set up LODs, click the Save button and close the window. Click Save All in the content drawer to save the imported assets. Double click on the MetaHuman blueprint. In the Component tab, add a Chaos Cloth component to the body. Select the cloth asset we just made. Compile and save. Playtest the level and see your Marvelous Designer garment simulate in real-time in Unreal Engine. Kill the rest of the back and create the whitening effect. Let the armor localize for a few seconds. Then add a new main element. Set the second layer color to black and let the gray color change to white. Use the mask to hide the color. Change the color to white. summary: ```markdown # USD to Unreal Engine Chaos Cloth Workflow Welcome to the tutorial on the USD to Unreal Engine Chaos Cloth Pipeline. In this guide, we will explore how to optimize garments created in Marvelous Designer for real-time simulation in Unreal Engine. ## Setting Up the Garment In this Marvelous Designer scene, I have fitted a dress created from the previous tutorial to the MetaHuman Female Medium Normal Weight Body Type. You can import default MetaHuman body types from the library. ### Optimizing for Real-Time Simulation To optimize this garment for real-time simulation in Unreal Engine, adjust the following settings: - **Increase Particle Distance**: Adjust this value to decrease mesh density. - **Add Collision Thickness**: Increase the collision thickness for the garment in Marvelous Designer. This value can be exported with the USD file and utilized in Unreal Engine. - **Thick Rendering Value**: Increase the thickness rendering value to add more thickness to the render mesh. ### Exporting the Garment 1. **Draping the Garment**: Turn on simulation to drape the garment with the modified properties. 2. **Exporting USD**: Go to `File > Export USD`. During the export, a render mesh with thickness and a separate single-sided simulation mesh will be generated for each full garment. In the export pop-up window: - Leave "Select All Avatars" checked. - Choose "Multiple Objects" and the "Thick" option. - Ensure you have laid out UVs for the garment and turn on the "Unified UV Coordinates" option. - A checkbox is available to include the necessary garment simulation data in the output for simulation setup in Unreal Engine Chaos Cloth. ## Importing into Unreal Engine 1. **Open Unreal Editor**: Add a cloth asset. A data flow asset with a default node graph preset will be automatically created. 2. **Open the Data Flow Node Graph**: Double-click to open the data flow node graph. ### Importing the USD File - Import the USD file exported from Marvelous Designer. - Use the **Transform Positions Node** to modify translation, rotation, and scale for both the render mesh and the simulation mesh. ### Transferring Skin Weights 1. **Select a Skeletal Mesh**: Use the **Transfer Skin Weights Node** to transfer skin weights to the simulation mesh. 2. **Weight Painting**: Paint the max distance using the **Add Weight Node**. The max distance informs how far the simulated cloth can move away from its animated skin position. You can weight paint in both 2D and 3D. ### Configuring Simulation Settings - **Max Distance Range**: Adjust the low and high values in the **Simulation Max Distance Config Node**. - **Fabric Settings**: The simulation config nodes allow you to set the fabric settings for the cloth materials. By default, they ingest the Marvelous Designer fabric parameters, but you can use custom values as needed. - **Enable Marvelous Designer Values**: The first blue toggle will enable the use of Marvelous Designer values, while the shirt icon will enable the weight map based on fabrics assigned in Marvelous Designer. ### Setting Up Physics 1. **Select a Physics Asset**: Use the **Set Physics Asset Node** and double-check if the physics asset has been correctly set up. 2. **Previewing Simulation**: In the Preview Scene Detail tab, select a skeletal mesh asset to preview the simulation. Click the **Toggle Simulation Suspended** button to toggle simulation on and off, and click the **Reset Simulation** button to reset the garment to the imported state. ### Collision and Aerodynamics - **Self-Collision**: By default, self-collision is disabled. You can activate the **Simulation Self-Collision Spheres Config Node** or use the **Simulation Self-Collision Config Node** for more precise self-collision. - **Simulation Solver Config Node**: Configure the iterations and sub-steps of the cloth simulation. - **Wind Force**: Set up wind force in the **Simulation Aerodynamics Config Node**. - **Collision Thickness**: In the **Simulation Collision Config Node**, turn on the blue toggle for collision thickness and use the value from the USD file exported from Marvelous Designer. ### Final Steps 1. **Set Up LODs**: Click the **Save** button and close the window. 2. **Save All Assets**: Click **Save All** in the content drawer to save the imported assets. 3. **Modify MetaHuman Blueprint**: Double-click on the MetaHuman blueprint. In the Component tab, add a **Chaos Cloth Component** to the body and select the cloth asset we just created. Compile and save. ## Testing the Simulation Playtest the level to see your Marvelous Designer garment simulate in real-time in Unreal Engine. - **Additional Effects**: Kill the rest of the back and create the whitening effect. Allow the armor to localize for a few seconds. - **Color Adjustments**: Add a new main element. Set the second layer color to black and let the gray color change to white. Use the mask to hide the color and reduce it to 0% to avoid further discoloration. Use the mask to move the object. --- This concludes the tutorial on the USD to Unreal Engine Chaos Cloth workflow. By following these steps, you can successfully create and simulate garments in Unreal Engine using data from Marvelous Designer. ```
